reporting-org.narrative: Obodo Centre for Advocacy and Equal Rights

description.narrative:
The library's mission is to offer a diverse and inclusive selection of books and resources that span genres and disciplines, addressing crucial themes such as human rights, African and LGBTQI+ history, cultural studies, psychology, and related fields. We are currently partnered with 3 bookstores/organizations to bring this initiative to fruition:
Gay's The Word The Common Press We Are Family Foundation
The Common Press and Gay's the Word Bookstores have both played instrumental roles in providing a varied selection of books, reflecting a wide spectrum of experiences and narratives. Commonpress is also generously offering a capacity-building resource to train library personnel, ensuring the effective management and operation of our Library and Resource Center. This comprehensive training will cover essential skills such as cataloging and classification, digital archiving, user services management, information literacy, collection development, and preservation techniques. Additionally, library personnel will gain knowledge in database management, reference services, community engagement, and the implementation of accessibility measures for diverse users. This training is vital for maintaining the integrity of our library's resources and ensuring that the centre remains a welcoming, well-organized space for all.
We Are Family Foundation has extended their support by facilitating access to a network of potential donors and resources. The London Metropolitan University has also committed to supporting the centre by providing access to academic papers online, further broadening the library's scope and enhancing its role as an educational and research resource.
A crucial component of the Library and Resource Centre initiative is the ongoing Book Drive which has received considerable support from the above-named bookstores/organizations by assisting with outreach efforts to ensure the drive reaches a broad audience, fostering greater community engagement and support.
The physical library is currently awaiting the arrival of the first shipment of books from Commonpress and Gay's the Word, which is in transit. This shipment represents the beginning of a growing collection that will continuously evolve to meet the needs of its users. The dual nature of the Library and Resource Center—offering both physical books and online resources—ensures that it can effectively cater to a diverse audience, making essential information and support accessible to all individuals regardless of their geographic location or other constraints. During this time, we have also started receiving donations from our community in Lagos, Nigeria. 843 persons have engaged with the Library and Resource Centre by reading about their history and associated topics and interacting with other community members through literary-focused activations to strengthen their knowledge.
The library currently houses 286 unique titles and a total of 522 items, including fiction and nonfiction books, as well as DVDs.
